AUTHOR: Villon
TITLE: A new method to control error rates in automated species identification with deep learning algorithms
REGION: Mayotte Island, Western Indian Ocean (fringing and barrier reefs)
SPECIES: 20 coral reef species incl. Chaetodon trifasciatus, C. trifascialis, C. guttatissimus, C. auriga, Naso brevirostris, N. elegans, Thalassoma hardwicke, Pomacentrus sulfureus, Oxymonacanthus longirostris, Monotaxis grandoculis, Zebrasoma scopas, Abudefduf vaigiensis, Amblyglyphidodon indicus, Acanthurus lineatus, A. leucosternon, Chromis ternatensis, C. opercularis, Gomphosus caeruleus, Halichoeres hortulanus, Zanclus cornutus
DATA: Own dataset: 175 GoPro HD videos (83 h); T0 training 130 videos / 69,169 cropped images (691,690 after augmentation); T1 threshold-tuning 20 videos / 6,320 images; T2 test 25 videos / 13,232 images
V_EV: Methods, Data: 'The videos were recorded between 2 and 30 m deep, with a broad range of luminosity, transparency, and benthic environment conditions'; no results stratified by condition
D2: T0 (130 videos, 69,169 images) / T1 (20 videos, 6,320) / T2 (25 videos, 13,232); T1 and T2 from different videos, days and sites than T0
D_EV: Methods, Data: 'two independent datasets made of different videos recorded on different days and on different sites than videos used to build the training dataset'; 'ensures that our results are not biased by similar acquisition conditions'
R_EV: Methods, Data: T1/T2 'recorded on different days and on different sites than videos used to build the training dataset' — same region (Mayotte); no in-domain vs. out-of-domain comparison reported
C_EV: Pure classification of pre-cropped single-fish images ('we cropped images to include only one fish individual'); confidence control via species-specific thresholds: 'for each species, a confidence threshold was automatically computed using a training dataset independent from the one used to train the DLAs'; Fig. 4/5 score-vs-correctness distributions and rates along a threshold gradient
E_EV: Results report only classification rates: 'The mean rate of correct classification of fish images in T2 by the raw CNN was of 78.0%'; misclassification/unsure rates and per-species accuracy (Tables 1-3); no ecological variable derived
ARCH: 100-layer ResNet (TensorFlow implementation), 64x64 input, softmax; post-hoc per-species confidence thresholds with 'unsure' class (three goal-specific threshold rules G1-G3)
METR: Correct classification rate (CC), misclassification rate (MC), unsure rate (UC), coverage, per-species accuracy (precision)
NOTE: Key confidence-control paper, but C_ALL = NA by the mechanical rule (pure classification of pre-cropped images, no detection/counting output); C1 = Y, C2 = 기타 (risk/coverage trade-off along thresholds, score-correctness violin plots, Fig. 4-5), C4 = Y are recorded so the verifier can override if confidence control in classification should count. R3 interpreted as 'in-domain vs. external performance compared'; T1/T2 differ from T0 in days and sites but are from the same region and camera, so R1 = Y is at the lower edge of 'external' — verifier may prefer R1 = N. MC rate (Eq. 2) is a per-class false-negative rate, hence E4 = FNR. Recording platform (diver vs. fixed GoPro) is not stated in the text (PLAT = NR; merged.json says DOV / fixed camera). FPS = Y refers to '5 frames per second' extraction, not camera frame rate. Pretraining not stated. NIMG = 69,169 + 6,320 + 13,232 native images (before augmentation). | C_ALL NA→Y (classification study with calibration/uncertainty analysis; amended rule). | POLICY: decision 2 — held-out days/sites within the same Mayotte campaign are not external.
